body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError in InvoiceSendButton sendInvoice, so invoices cannot be sent
body.summary: The user opened a new invoice, entered a customer and amount, saved a draft, and then clicked Send invoice. The send action threw a TypeError, and the user rage-clicked the Send invoice button without the invoice being sent.
body.expected: The invoice is sent after clicking Send invoice.
body.actual: Clicking Send invoice raises TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21), and the user then rage-clicks #send-invoice five times.

evidence.note: The uncaught TypeError at sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21) is the primary failure.
The same error is logged to the console, confirming it occurs on the send click.
Five rapid clicks on #send-invoice show the user repeatedly retrying a button that does nothing.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that sendInvoice reads the .id property of a value that is undefined at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48, possibly because the customer or saved draft object is not available when Send is clicked.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') @ InvoiceSendButton.tsx

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: The user opened invoice inv_8812 and clicked Send reminder twice, at 00:03 and 00:07. Each click sent POST /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders, which returned 500 internal_error and displayed "Something went wrong. Please try again."
body.expected: Clicking Send reminder sends the payment reminder for the invoice without error.
body.actual: The reminders request returns 500 internal_error and the user sees "Something went wrong. Please try again." Retrying the click produces the same result.

evidence.note: Primary failure: the reminders POST returns 500 internal_error after the first click.
The user sees the generic error message after the first failed request.
The same endpoint fails with 500 again on the second click, so the failure is repeatable.
The generic error message is shown again after the retry.

body.suspected_cause: A likely server-side exception in the reminders endpoint for this invoice, since the API returns internal_error on each attempt.

body.title: AR aging report times out with 504 on /reports, showing 'taking too long' message
body.summary: The user opened the reports page and clicked AR aging, expecting the report to load. The aging request timed out after about 30 seconds with a 504, and the user saw a 'taking too long' message after repeatedly clicking the report link.
body.expected: The AR aging report loads and displays.
body.actual: The aging request returned a 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, and the user saw 'This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range.'

evidence.note: Primary failure: GET /api/reports/aging returned 504 after 30012 ms.
User rage-clicked the AR aging link four times while waiting, suggesting no progress feedback.
User was shown a timeout message suggesting a shorter range, which the user did not select.

body.suspected_cause: The aging report query likely exceeds the gateway's 30-second timeout, possibly because the default range is too large or the query is slow.

body.title: Payments page fails to load: JS chunk 812 returns 404 after deploy
body.summary: The user opened the dashboard and clicked Payments to open /payments. The page failed to load because the chunk file /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404, and the user saw "Page failed to load."
body.expected: The Payments page loads and displays normally.
body.actual: The request GET /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404, a ChunkLoadError was thrown for chunk 812, and the user saw "Page failed to load."

evidence.note: The chunk request returned 404, which is the primary failure.
ChunkLoadError confirms the page's JavaScript chunk could not be loaded.
The error message shown to the user confirms the page did not load.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that the 812 chunk filename referenced by the deployed app no longer exists on the server, such as a stale or mismatched asset after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy.

body.body: +1 from another session (Chrome 141, app 2026.10.27-2): POST /api/invoices/inv_7731/pdf -> 500 in 2800 ms (pdf_render_failed) at [00:02]. Replay: https://us.posthog.com/project/102/replay/rec_07_pdf_dup?t=0

body.title: Customers CSV export fails with 500 from /api/customers/export on the customers page
body.summary: The user opened the customers page with a search applied and then clicked Export CSV. The export request returned a 500 with export_failed, and the user saw an "Export failed." message.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page (/customers) with a search query applied.

body.expected: The customer list exports as a CSV file.
body.actual: The export request returns HTTP 500 (export_failed) and the user sees "Export failed."

evidence.note: The export request to /api/customers/export returned 500 with export_failed, which is the primary failure.
The console logged the export failure as a 500 error.
The user was shown the generic "Export failed." message.

body.suspected_cause: The server-side export handler likely fails when processing the export request, possibly due to the email filter parameter in the query.

body.title: QuickBooks sync fails with 500 when clicking Sync now on /settings/integrations
body.summary: On the integrations settings page, the user clicked Sync now to start a QuickBooks sync. The sync request returned a 500 after about 5 seconds and the user saw a 'Sync failed' message.
body.expected: The QuickBooks sync completes without error.
body.actual: The sync request fails with a 500 status after about 5100 ms, and the user sees 'Sync failed. We'll retry automatically.'

evidence.note: The POST to /api/integrations/quickbooks/sync returned 500 with sync_failed, which is the primary failure.
The user was shown a sync failure message, confirming the error reached the UI.

body.suspected_cause: The server-side QuickBooks sync handler likely threw an unhandled error, since the request returned 500 with a sync_failed code after a long delay.

body.title: Revenue report fails with RangeError when applying a custom date range
body.summary: The user opened the revenue report and set a custom date range via the date picker, then clicked Apply. The report failed with an error message and the Apply button was rage-clicked repeatedly.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Type a value into the start date field.
Click Apply to apply the range.

body.expected: The report applies the selected date range and reloads the revenue data.
body.actual: The report shows "Something went wrong loading this report." A RangeError: Invalid time value is thrown in formatDateRange, and the user rage-clicks Apply.

evidence.note: Uncaught RangeError in formatDateRange is the primary failure.
Console confirms the same Invalid time value error.
User-facing error message shown on the report page.
Repeated clicks on Apply suggest the user was stuck and the action did not recover.

body.suspected_cause: The date range picker likely passes an unparseable or empty start date into formatDateRange, producing an Invalid Date that throws a RangeError.

body.title: Payments page crashes with TypeError in formatRow when Refunds filter is clicked
body.summary: The user opened the Payments page and clicked the Refunds filter (#filter-refunds). The app threw a TypeError reading 'amount' from null in formatRow and displayed the generic error 'Something went wrong.' Same signature as BUG-280 (closed); likely a regression.
body.expected: The Refunds filter should show the refund rows in the payments table without an error.
body.actual: The payments view fails with a TypeError (Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount') at formatRow in PaymentsTable.tsx:77:30) and the user sees 'Something went wrong.'

evidence.note: Uncaught TypeError shows formatRow dereferences a null row or value when the Refunds filter is applied.
The user-facing error message confirms the payments view failed to render.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that formatRow in PaymentsTable.tsx receives a null entry for refund rows and reads .amount without a null check.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount') @ PaymentsTable.tsx
